canonical_criteria.requirement: Gate 1 — FORMULA: Explicit statement of the governing physical law or equation before any substitution.
accepted_equivalents: Standard textbook form of the equation
Rearranged algebraic equivalent provided derivation shown
insufficient_alone: Jumping directly to substitution without stating the formula
Writing only the final answer

evaluation_examples.context: Concave lens focal length via lens formula
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Directly writing 1/f = 1/(-30) - 1/(-45) without first stating the general formula
Omitting the formula and writing only the arithmetic

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Heat lost = Heat gained; ml + mcΔt = mcΔt
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Writing mcΔt = ml as the starting equation (incorrect LHS/RHS assignment)

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Sum of clockwise moments = Sum of anticlockwise moments
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Writing only the substituted equation without stating the principle

canonical_criteria.requirement: Gate 2 — SUBSTITUTION: All given values substituted into the formula with uniform units (SI or CGS consistently) and correct sign conventions.
insufficient_alone: Mixing SI and CGS units in the same equation
Omitting sign convention in optics (all distances positive)
Converting specific heat capacity to SI but leaving mass in CGS

evaluation_examples.context: Concave lens: u = -45 cm, v = -30 cm
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Using positive values for u and v with a concave lens

evaluation_examples.context: Calorimetry mixing SI specific heat with CGS mass
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: 30(336 + 4.2 × 20) = m × 4.2 × 50 with all values in grams and J/g°C
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Converting c and l to SI while leaving mass in grams without conversion

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: 1 J = 1 kg·m/s² × 1 m then converting each to CGS equivalents
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Mixing kg and g in the same substitution line

canonical_criteria.requirement: Gate 3 — FINAL_VALUE_AND_UNIT: Final numerical magnitude expressed as a decimal or whole number (never as an unsimplified fraction) with the correct SI or CGS unit explicitly written.
insufficient_alone: Final value without unit
Unsimplified fraction as final answer (e.g., 8/5, 41/4, -1/90)
Bare numeral without dimensional unit
Correct value with wrong unit

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: f = -90 cm
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: -90 (unit missing) or leaving as -1/90
303 without 'K' unit
75000 without unit, or leaving as 1500 × 100 / 2 unsimplified

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: v = +24 cm
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: 24 without cm, or leaving as 24/1

evaluation_examples.context: Kinetic energy calculation with kgf to N conversion
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: 2000 without J, or incorrect kgf-to-N conversion yielding wrong magnitude

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Final numerical answer without unit
negative_constraints.correct_form: Magnitude accompanied by correct SI/CGS unit
negative_constraints.context: Any numerical sub-question producing a dimensional physical quantity

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Final answer left as an unsimplified or improper fraction
negative_constraints.correct_form: Express final answer in decimal form
negative_constraints.context: All numerical problems except pure ratio/dimensionless comparisons

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Mixing SI and CGS units in a single substitution step
negative_constraints.correct_form: All terms in uniform SI or uniform CGS system before arithmetic

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Incorrect sign convention in optics (treating all distances as positive)
negative_constraints.correct_form: Apply Cartesian sign convention: distances measured from optic centre, real-object side negative for u, same-side virtual image negative for v
negative_constraints.context: Lens formula and mirror formula numericals

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Writing mcΔt = ml or mcΔt = mcΔt as the calorimetry starting equation
negative_constraints.correct_form: Heat lost by hot body = Heat gained by cold body, with ml term on the correct side for phase change

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Incorrect conversion of kilogram-force to newton or gram
negative_constraints.correct_form: 1 kgf = 9.8 N ≈ 10 N (as given); mass in kgf must be multiplied by g to get weight in N

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Not converting minutes to seconds before substituting into v = 2d/t
negative_constraints.correct_form: Convert all time to seconds: 1 min 40 s = 100 s

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Neglecting the moment due to the weight of the ruler in equilibrium problems involving uniform rulers
negative_constraints.correct_form: Include the ruler's own weight acting at its centre of gravity (midpoint for uniform ruler) when calculating moments
negative_constraints.context: Principle of moments with uniform metre rule

archetypes.name: Ray Diagrams Through Prisms and Lenses
trigger_patterns: Show the path of the ray

canonical_criteria.requirement: All incident, refracted, and emergent rays must carry directional arrowheads indicating the direction of propagation of light.
insufficient_alone: Rays drawn without any arrows
Arrow on only one ray

evaluation_examples.context: TIR ray diagram through right-angled prism
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: All three ray segments (incident, internally reflected, emergent) carry arrowheads
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Correct path drawn but arrows missing — mark voided

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Arrows on incident ray entering prism and emergent ray leaving prism
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: No arrows drawn on any ray

canonical_criteria.requirement: Angles of incidence, reflection, and refraction must be measured from the NORMAL to the surface, never from the optical surface or prism face.
insufficient_alone: Angle measured from the prism face or lens surface
Normal not drawn

evaluation_examples.context: Angle of incidence at prism face
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Normal drawn perpendicular to prism face at point of incidence; angle measured between incoming ray and normal
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Angle measured between incoming ray and prism face

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Normal at hypotenuse face; angle of incidence from normal = 45° for TIR
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Measuring angle from the hypotenuse surface

canonical_criteria.requirement: Real rays and real images must be drawn as solid continuous lines. Virtual rays, backward extensions, and virtual images must be drawn as dashed or dotted lines.
insufficient_alone: All lines solid including virtual extensions
Dotted lines used for real rays
No distinction between real and virtual paths

evaluation_examples.context: Convex lens ray diagram with object at 2F — real image
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: All construction rays solid; image indicated at 2F on opposite side with solid lines
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Using dotted lines for real rays of light

evaluation_examples.context: Convex lens with object between O and F — virtual image
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Real rays solid; backward extensions dashed; virtual image dashed
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Virtual image shown as solid lines

canonical_criteria.requirement: For lens diagrams, the object must be placed at the correct position relative to the optical centre, and the scale must be uniform on both sides of the lens.
insufficient_alone: Object placed at arbitrary position regardless of question specification
Non-uniform scale across the lens

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Object placed exactly at 2F with equal scale markings F and 2F on both sides
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Object not drawn at 2F, or non-uniform scale

canonical_criteria.requirement: For prism TIR diagrams, the ray must undergo total internal reflection at the correct face, with angle of incidence at that face exceeding the critical angle.
insufficient_alone: Ray shown refracting through the TIR face instead of reflecting
TIR at the wrong face of the prism

evaluation_examples.context: Right-angled prism with TIR at hypotenuse
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Ray enters one short face normally, hits hypotenuse at 45° (> critical angle), totally reflects, exits other short face
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Ray shown refracting through hypotenuse

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: TIR at hypotenuse; emergent ray perpendicular to incident ray
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Ray path does not show 90° total deviation

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Ray diagram drawn without directional arrowheads on rays
negative_constraints.correct_form: Every ray segment must carry an arrowhead indicating direction of light propagation
negative_constraints.context: All ray diagrams — prisms, lenses, slabs, TIR

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Angle of incidence or refraction measured from the optical surface instead of the normal
negative_constraints.correct_form: All angles measured from the normal drawn perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence
negative_constraints.context: Any refraction or reflection at prism, lens, or slab surface

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Virtual image or virtual ray extension drawn with solid continuous lines
negative_constraints.correct_form: Virtual components drawn as dashed or dotted lines; real components as solid lines
negative_constraints.context: Diverging lens images, virtual images formed by converging lens (object between O and F)

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Using arrows on virtual ray extensions
negative_constraints.correct_form: Virtual ray extensions (backward projections) should be dashed lines without arrowheads; only real ray segments carry arrows
negative_constraints.context: Virtual image formation in diverging lenses or mirrors

canonical_criteria.requirement: Correct identification of live, neutral, and earth wires by their standard colour codes and functional roles in household wiring.
insufficient_alone: Naming colours without associating to wire function
Reversing live and neutral assignments

evaluation_examples.context: Wire colour identification in household wiring
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Live = Red/Brown, Neutral = Black/Blue, Earth = Green/Green-Yellow
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Swapping Live and Neutral colours

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Correct colour-wire-function triplet
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Naming colours without wire function

canonical_criteria.requirement: In meter room diagrams, correctly identify the fuse rating (based on load), distinguish between double-pole (main) switch and single-pole switches, and identify the unit of the meter reading.
insufficient_alone: Writing the fuse rating of the distribution system instead of the company fuse
Confusing double-pole switch with dual control switch
Confusing kW with kWh

evaluation_examples.context: Current rating of device X in meter room
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: 50 A (company's main fuse rating)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Writing the ring distribution fuse rating instead

evaluation_examples.context: Difference between switch Z (double pole) and home switches (single pole)
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Switch Z is in live and neutral (double pole); home switch is in live only (single pole)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Calling Z a dual control switch or MCB

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: kWh (kilowatt hour)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Writing kW or joules

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Confusing the company's main fuse rating with the ring circuit fuse rating
negative_constraints.correct_form: Identify the correct fuse based on its position in the wiring hierarchy (company fuse vs distribution board fuse)

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Confusing double-pole switch with dual control switch or MCB
negative_constraints.correct_form: Double-pole switch breaks both live and neutral; single-pole switch breaks only live

canonical_criteria.requirement: Diagram must show correct number of pulleys distributed between fixed upper block and movable lower block, with VR equal to the number of supporting strands on the load.
accepted_equivalents: For odd VR: one more pulley in fixed block than movable block
For even VR: equal number of pulleys in fixed and movable blocks
insufficient_alone: Incorrect number of pulleys
All pulleys in one block

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: 2 pulleys in fixed block, 1 in movable block; 3 supporting strands on load
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: 3 pulleys all in one block

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Correct distribution with 3 taut strands supporting the load
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Pulleys connected from rim instead of axle

canonical_criteria.requirement: All strings must be drawn taut and straight, with upward tension arrows (T) marked uniformly on every supporting strand.
insufficient_alone: Loose or curved strings
Tension arrows missing or not uniform
Tension marked as T₁, T₂, T₃ with different values on strands of same tackle

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Each of 3 strands has upward arrow labeled T; strings taut and straight
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Loose strands; or marking T₁, T₂, T₃ separately suggesting unequal tensions

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Taut strings with uniform T arrows
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Loose strings hanging from pulleys

canonical_criteria.requirement: Load (L) must hang from the movable block with a downward arrow. Effort (E) must be applied at the free end of the string with a labeled arrow.
insufficient_alone: Load and effort labels missing
Load shown on fixed block

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: L with downward arrow below movable block; E with downward arrow on free string end
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: No labels for L or E

canonical_criteria.requirement: Fixed block must be attached to a clearly drawn rigid support (beam/ceiling). Pulleys in fixed block must be connected through their axles, not from the rim.
insufficient_alone: No rigid support shown
Pulleys connected from rim or hooks on rim

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Rigid beam drawn above; pulleys axle-mounted to beam
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Main support not drawn; pulleys floating

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Clearly labeled rigid support
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Hooks connected from rim of pulleys

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Loose or sagging strings in pulley diagram
negative_constraints.correct_form: All strings taut and straight between pulleys

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Tension arrows missing or marked with different magnitudes on strands of the same tackle
negative_constraints.correct_form: Uniform upward tension T on every supporting strand of a single continuous string

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Pulleys connected from rim instead of axle in fixed block
negative_constraints.correct_form: Pulleys mounted through axle to the rigid support

archetypes.name: Nuclear Reactions and Radioactive Decay
trigger_patterns: What is the value of X

canonical_criteria.requirement: Correct identification of the nuclear process (fission, fusion, or specific decay type) based on the reaction equation or graphical representation.
insufficient_alone: Writing 'nuclear reaction' without specifying fission or fusion
Writing 'radioactive reaction' or 'chain reaction' as a substitute for fission
Confusing fission with fusion

evaluation_examples.context: Nuclear fission diagram with U-235 + neutron → Ba + Kr + 3 neutrons + energy
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Nuclear fission
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: 'Nuclear fusion' or 'radioactive reaction' or 'chain reaction'

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Fission: heavy nucleus splits; Fusion: light nuclei combine
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Reversing the definitions

canonical_criteria.requirement: Conservation of mass number (A) and atomic number (Z) must be satisfied across the nuclear equation. The sum of mass numbers on LHS must equal the sum on RHS; likewise for atomic numbers.
insufficient_alone: Balanced atomic number but unbalanced mass number
Correct product but wrong mass number due to not counting the captured neutron

evaluation_examples.context: Find X in: U-235 + n → X_92_U → Ba-144 + Kr-89 + 3n
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: X = 236 (235 + 1 = 236, accounting for the absorbed neutron)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: X = 235 (forgetting the captured neutron adds to mass number)

evaluation_examples.context: Nuclear decay from graph — identify daughter nucleus after alpha/beta emissions
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Correct mass and atomic number after accounting for each emission
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Position in periodic table after alpha decay incorrectly placed (wrong element group)

canonical_criteria.requirement: Missing particles must be identified with correct notation: neutron as ₀¹n, alpha as ₂⁴He or ₂⁴α, beta as ₋₁⁰e or ₋₁⁰β.
insufficient_alone: Identifying a neutron as alpha or beta particle
Using wrong notation (e.g., writing neutron with charge)

evaluation_examples.context: Identify Y — missing product in fission equation
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: 3 neutrons / ₀¹n
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Identifying missing particle as alpha or beta

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Confusing nuclear fission with fusion or writing 'chain reaction' as the process name
negative_constraints.correct_form: Fission = heavy nucleus splits into lighter fragments; Fusion = light nuclei combine into heavier nucleus
negative_constraints.context: Naming nuclear processes from equations or diagrams

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Not adding the mass of the captured neutron to the intermediate nucleus mass number
negative_constraints.correct_form: When a nucleus absorbs a neutron, the intermediate mass number = original mass number + 1

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Confusing position shift in periodic table after alpha decay (moving left 2 places) with beta decay (moving right 1 place)
negative_constraints.correct_form: Alpha: Z decreases by 2, A decreases by 4; Beta: Z increases by 1, A unchanged
negative_constraints.context: Radioactive decay series and nuclear transmutation

canonical_criteria.requirement: Response must contain the specific scientific principle, law, or physical mechanism that explains the phenomenon — not a restatement of the observation.
insufficient_alone: Restating the observation as the reason
Circular reasoning (e.g., 'it happens because it happens')
Vague qualitative claims without physical basis

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Light must travel from denser to rarer medium AND angle of incidence must exceed the critical angle
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Only stating one condition, or confusing denser/rarer direction

evaluation_examples.context: Why centripetal force needed for circular motion
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: To continuously change the direction of velocity while maintaining uniform speed; force directed toward centre
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Writing centrifugal force instead of centripetal

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Resonance: tuning fork frequency matches the natural frequency of wire B, causing it to vibrate with maximum amplitude — paper rider falls off
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Stating tuning fork frequency equals frequency of the paper rider or the wooden box

canonical_criteria.requirement: For resonance questions, two explicit anchors are mandatory: (a) driving frequency matches the natural frequency of the vibrating body, and (b) the body vibrates with maximum or increased amplitude.
insufficient_alone: Only stating frequency match without amplitude increase
Stating the tuning fork frequency equals the frequency of the paper rider or box
Omitting the concept of natural frequency

evaluation_examples.context: Resonance — paper rider falls off wire B
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: The tuning fork's frequency matches the natural frequency of wire on box B; wire B vibrates with maximum amplitude, dislodging the rider
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Saying tuning fork frequency = paper rider frequency

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: When tuning fork frequency matches natural frequency of the wire, wire vibrates with maximum amplitude (resonance)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Writing that the wire vibrates 'at the same frequency as the tuning fork' without mentioning natural frequency or amplitude increase

canonical_criteria.requirement: For TIR justification, two conditions must be stated: (a) light travels from optically denser to optically rarer medium, AND (b) angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.
insufficient_alone: Only one condition stated
Reversing medium direction (rarer to denser)
Writing 'angle of incidence equals critical angle' instead of 'exceeds'

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Light travels from denser to rarer medium; angle of incidence > critical angle
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Missing either condition

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Both conditions stated with correct directionality
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Defining critical angle without specifying denser-to-rarer requirement

canonical_criteria.requirement: For phase-change reasoning, the response must state that temperature remains constant because absorbed heat increases the potential energy of molecules while average kinetic energy remains strictly constant.
insufficient_alone: Simply stating 'temperature remains constant during melting'
Saying 'heat is used to break bonds' without mentioning PE and KE

evaluation_examples.context: Why temperature remains constant during melting
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Heat absorbed increases PE of molecules to overcome intermolecular forces; average KE (and therefore temperature) stays constant
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Only saying 'latent heat is absorbed' without the PE/KE mechanism

canonical_criteria.requirement: For electromagnetic force effect questions, the reasoning must connect the physical variable (cross-sectional area, current, field strength, length) to force via the governing formula F = BIl.
insufficient_alone: Simply applying F = BIlsinθ and saying 'no effect' because area is not in the formula
Listing factors without connecting to the formula
Not recognizing that greater cross-section reduces resistance and thus increases current

evaluation_examples.context: Effect on force when rod cross-section increases
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Force increases because greater cross-sectional area → lower resistance → greater current → greater F (since F = BIl and I increases)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Saying 'no effect' because area is not directly in F = BIl

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Writing centrifugal force instead of centripetal force for circular motion
negative_constraints.correct_form: Centripetal force is directed toward the centre; centrifugal is a pseudo-force in rotating frame

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Equating tuning fork frequency to paper rider or wooden box frequency in resonance
negative_constraints.correct_form: Tuning fork (driving) frequency matches natural frequency of the vibrating wire/string

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Confusing 'turning the glass upside down' with an increase in real depth in real/apparent depth problems
negative_constraints.correct_form: Ratio of real to apparent depth is constant (equals refractive index); when real depth changes, apparent depth changes proportionally

archetypes.name: Formal Definitions of Laws and Physical Quantities

canonical_criteria.requirement: Definition must contain ALL mandatory key phrases specified in the marking scheme. Missing any single key phrase voids the mark for that phrase.
accepted_equivalents: Semantically equivalent phrasing that preserves the physical meaning
insufficient_alone: Partial definition missing a critical qualifier
Circular definition
Example given instead of definition

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: The turning effect of a force about a point is the product of the force and the PERPENDICULAR DISTANCE from the point to the line of action of the force
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Writing 'distance' instead of 'perpendicular distance'

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Vibrations of a body at its natural frequency WITHOUT any external periodic force
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Omitting 'without external periodic force'

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Atoms of DIFFERENT elements having the SAME mass number but DIFFERENT atomic numbers
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Confusing with isotopes (same element, different mass number)

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: The phenomenon by which a beam of light is redirected in different directions when it interacts with particles of the medium
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Confusing scattering with refraction or dispersion

canonical_criteria.requirement: For moment of force: the term 'perpendicular distance' is non-negotiable. Writing 'distance' alone scores zero.
accepted_equivalents: perpendicular distance from the axis/point/fulcrum to the line of action of force
insufficient_alone: 'distance' without 'perpendicular'
'shortest distance' (ambiguous)

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Force × perpendicular distance from the fulcrum
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Force × distance (missing 'perpendicular') = 0 marks

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Omitting 'perpendicular' in the definition of moment of force
negative_constraints.correct_form: Moment = Force × perpendicular distance from the pivot/fulcrum
negative_constraints.context: Definition of moment of force / torque

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Omitting 'without external periodic force' in definition of free vibrations
negative_constraints.correct_form: Free vibrations: body vibrates at its natural frequency without any external periodic force after being displaced and released

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Confusing isobars (same A, different Z) with isotopes (same Z, different A)
negative_constraints.correct_form: Isobars: different elements, same mass number; Isotopes: same element, different mass numbers

archetypes.name: Identification of Physical Quantities, Radiations, and Conversions

canonical_criteria.requirement: The identified item must match the official marking scheme terminology exactly or be an accepted equivalent listed in the scheme.
accepted_equivalents: Full name or standard abbreviation as listed in marking scheme
insufficient_alone: A related but incorrect term
A subjective description instead of the standard name

evaluation_examples.context: Name radiations: quartz prism spectrum, remote sensing, traffic signals
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: 1. Ultraviolet/UV rays; 2. Infrared/IR radiations/microwaves/radio waves; 3. Visible light (any colour)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Confusing UV with ultrasonic; confusing IR with infrasonic

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Correct 'input energy → output energy' format
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Reversing input and output energies

evaluation_examples.context: Name the law for direction of motion of current-carrying conductor in magnetic field
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule / Right Hand Palm Rule
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Fleming's Right-Hand Rule / Thumb Rule / Faraday's Law / Lenz's Law

canonical_criteria.requirement: For specific heat capacity comparison questions, the material with LOWER specific heat capacity shows HIGHER temperature rise for the same heat input, and is selected for making a calorimeter due to low heat absorption.
insufficient_alone: Stating higher temperature rise means higher specific heat capacity
Selecting the material with higher SHC for calorimeter

evaluation_examples.context: Material X warms 10°C, material Y warms 40°C for same heat and mass
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: X has higher SHC (lower temp rise); Y selected for calorimeter (low SHC = absorbs less heat)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Saying Y has higher SHC because it has higher temperature rise

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Confusing ultraviolet with ultrasonic, or infrared with infrasonic
negative_constraints.correct_form: UV/IR are electromagnetic radiations; ultrasonic/infrasonic are sound waves

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Confusing Fleming's Left-Hand Rule with Fleming's Right-Hand Rule
negative_constraints.correct_form: Left-Hand Rule for motor effect (force on current-carrying conductor in magnetic field); Right-Hand Rule for dynamo/generator effect

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Confusing electromagnetic radiation properties with radioactive radiation properties
negative_constraints.correct_form: Electromagnetic radiations share properties: travel at speed of light in vacuum, no medium required, can refract/reflect. Radioactive emissions have particle nature (alpha, beta) or are a specific EM ray (gamma).
negative_constraints.context: Common property identification for EM radiations

canonical_criteria.requirement: Response must present matched pairs of contrasting properties — each distinguishing point for item A must have a corresponding contrasting point for item B on the same criterion.
insufficient_alone: Listing properties of only one item
Non-parallel comparison (different criteria for A and B)
Repeating the same point in different words

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Fission: heavy nucleus → lighter fragments + energy; Fusion: light nuclei → heavier nucleus + energy
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Only describing fission without the matching fusion counterpart

evaluation_examples.context: Heat capacity vs specific heat capacity
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Heat capacity: heat to raise temp of whole body by 1°C (unit: J/°C); SHC: heat to raise temp of unit mass by 1°C (unit: J/kg°C)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Defining only one term

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Switch Z in live AND neutral (double pole); home switch in live ONLY (single pole)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Calling Z a dual control switch

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Listing properties of only one item without the contrasting counterpart
negative_constraints.correct_form: Each point about A must have a matching contrasting point about B

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Confusing heat capacity (whole body) with specific heat capacity (per unit mass)
negative_constraints.correct_form: Heat capacity = mcΔθ/Δθ = mc (for the body); SHC = c (per unit mass per degree)
negative_constraints.context: Heat capacity vs specific heat capacity distinction

canonical_criteria.requirement: For sound wave comparison, correctly identify which waveform has greater amplitude (louder) and which has shorter wavelength/higher frequency (higher pitch) based on visual inspection of the waveforms.
insufficient_alone: Confusing amplitude with wavelength
Using subjective descriptors (softer/quieter) instead of objective quantities (amplitude/frequency)

evaluation_examples.context: Two sound waveforms — compare amplitude and wavelength
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Wave A has larger amplitude (louder); Wave B has shorter wavelength (higher pitch/frequency)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Saying Wave A has higher pitch because it has larger amplitude

evaluation_examples.context: Sound wave graph — identify amplitude and wavelength changes
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Correctly marking amplitude on displacement axis and wavelength along time/distance axis
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Measuring amplitude as peak-to-peak instead of zero-to-peak

canonical_criteria.requirement: For nuclear decay graphs, correctly read mass number and atomic number from axes to identify the parent and daughter nuclei and the type of decay.
insufficient_alone: Reading graph values incorrectly
Confusing mass number axis with atomic number axis

evaluation_examples.context: Nuclear decay graph — read values and identify decay type
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Reading initial and final (A, Z) values; identifying alpha decay (A decreases by 4, Z by 2) or beta decay (Z increases by 1, A same)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Misreading the graph axes or confusing decay types

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Confusing pitch (frequency) with loudness (amplitude) or using them interchangeably
negative_constraints.correct_form: Pitch is determined by frequency; Loudness is determined by amplitude. These are independent physical quantities.

archetypes.name: Lever Class Identification and Mechanical Advantage

canonical_criteria.requirement: Lever class identification based on the relative positions of Load (L), Fulcrum (F), and Effort (E): Class I = F between L and E; Class II = L between F and E; Class III = E between F and L.
insufficient_alone: Naming the class without relating to L, F, E positions when justification is required
Confusing classes when multiple lever diagrams share the same class

evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Class II lever — load between fulcrum and effort
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Misidentifying the class due to incorrect L/F/E positions

evaluation_examples.context: Three levers X, Y, Z of equal length — identify class
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Class I / First class lever (all three have fulcrum between load and effort)
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Saying each is a different class

canonical_criteria.requirement: For maximum mechanical advantage identification, the lever with the longest effort arm relative to load arm gives maximum MA. MA = Effort Arm / Load Arm.
insufficient_alone: Stating 'highest effort arm' without comparing to load arm
Confusing effort arm with load arm

evaluation_examples.context: Among levers X, Y, Z of equal length, which gives maximum MA
evaluation_examples.sample_hit: Lever X — effort arm is longest relative to load arm (EA > LA), so MA = EA/LA is greatest
evaluation_examples.sample_penalty: Identifying the lever with highest effort arm alone without comparing to load arm

negative_constraints.wrong_form: Claiming multiple lever diagrams belong to different classes when they all share the same fulcrum-load-effort arrangement
negative_constraints.correct_form: If all levers have fulcrum between load and effort, all are Class I regardless of exact positions

global_negative_constraints.wrong_form: Leaving final answers in fractional form (e.g., 8/5, 41/4, -1/90)
global_negative_constraints.correct_form: Express final answer in decimal form up to appropriate decimal places
global_negative_constraints.context: All numerical problems except pure ratio or dimensionless comparison questions

global_negative_constraints.wrong_form: Omitting units from dimensional physical quantities in final answers
global_negative_constraints.correct_form: Every dimensional final answer must carry the correct SI or CGS unit
global_negative_constraints.context: All numerical sub-questions producing dimensional quantities

evidence.question_ref: General Comments — Suggestions for candidates: 'Pay attention to writing correct units for all physical quantities'

global_negative_constraints.wrong_form: Missing directional arrowheads on rays in any optical diagram
global_negative_constraints.correct_form: Every ray segment in a ray diagram must carry a directional arrowhead
global_negative_constraints.context: All ray-optics diagrams — prisms, lenses, slabs, mirrors

evidence.question_ref: General Comments — Suggestions for candidates: 'Always draw arrows on rays'

global_negative_constraints.wrong_form: Drawing neat diagrams without labels for forces, tensions, loads, efforts, or key components
global_negative_constraints.correct_form: All diagrams must have appropriate labels for physical quantities and components
global_negative_constraints.context: All diagrammatic questions including pulleys, levers, circuits, and ray diagrams

global_negative_constraints.wrong_form: Using subjective sound descriptors (louder/softer/shrill) as physical quantities
global_negative_constraints.correct_form: Pitch is governed by frequency (Hz); Loudness is governed by amplitude. Use objective physical quantities.

global_negative_constraints.wrong_form: Confusing resistance with resistivity in circuit analysis
global_negative_constraints.correct_form: Resistance (R) is for a specific conductor; Resistivity (ρ) is a material property. R = ρl/A
